title: Software LMUL Templates
description: Bodies of the functions that change a software LMUL, written by one ISA (`simd_ext/<isa>/<isa>_sw_lmul.json`, optional): `wcvt` from `m1` to `m2` and `ncvt` from `m2` to `m1`, for an ISA whose LMUL > 1 registers are software ones (`sw_lmul` in the [ISA Descriptor](isa.md), a struct of two LMUL 1 registers `lo` and `hi`). Without this file, the generator writes generic bodies (`codegen/lmul_orchestrator.py`): `wcvt` converts each half of the argument (`lo` / `hi`, then the `d2` -> `m1` conversion of [Half-Vector Templates](ldiv_mask.md)) and `ncvt` joins the conversions of the two registers with `combine`. An ISA gives its own body when it has better instructions (SVE: `svunpklo` / `svunpkhi`, `svuzp1`); the higher LMULs (`m2` -> `m4`, ...) call these functions on each half. The code is Jinja2 and [templating DSL](../templating_dsl.md), rendered for the LMUL of the arguments (`m1` for `wcvt`, `m2` for `ncvt`): `%vd<tr>%` is the type of the result. Each key is a function name. See [Code Generation](../../internals/code_generation.md#2-one-isa-layer) and [Add an ISA](../../tutorials/add_isa.md#half-vectors-and-functions-that-change-the-lmul).

level.description: Implementation level shown in the generated `// Level` comment. Optional. Without it, the level is detected from the code with the rules of the level audit (0: a single intrinsic; 1: several intrinsics, or intrinsics and MIPP functions; 2: only MIPP functions).

datatypes.description: Datatypes of the argument the entry applies to, or `all_datatypes` (the default). The first matching entry is used; a datatype without an entry keeps the generic body.

code.description: Body of the function, one line per item: Jinja2 (variables `isa`, `isa_dt` for the datatype entry of the argument in the ISA descriptor, `ctx` with `ctx.dt_par` / `ctx.dt_ret`, ...) and templating DSL (`%vd<tr>%` for the result). The result has the registers `res.lo` / `res.hi` for `wcvt`, the argument has `vd0.lo` / `vd0.hi` for `ncvt`.

additionalProperties.description: Entries of the function, tried in order.
